body:
WHAT
The TUI is MAGENTRA's terminal user interface (a text UI that runs inside a shell instead of the Electron desktop window). When the TUI ships inside the desktop install it lives at resources/engine/tui.mjs next to the bundled engine file engine.cjs. In that case it starts the engine by running engine.cjs with the Electron binary itself, using the environment flag ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 so Electron behaves as plain Node. In a development checkout it instead reads ~/.magentra-tui.json for an engineHome and runs engine/host/dist/main.js with the system node.

WHY
An installed machine has no system Node and no repo checkout, so a packaged TUI that looked for either would fail to start; the only Node available is the one inside Electron, and the only engine is the sibling bundle.

WHERE
tui/src/config.ts — constants bundleDir/packagedEngine, isPackagedRun(), resolveEngineSpawn(workspace) (packaged branch returns command=process.execPath, args=[engine.cjs, --cwd, ws], env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE='1'; dev branch uses loadConfig()/hostEntry()), CONFIG_PATH, guessEngineHome(); tui/src/cli.tsx — entry that renders <App>, imports isPackagedRun; tui/src/engine/useEngine.ts — the useEffect that calls resolveEngineSpawn and boot(), shutdown() → host.kill(); tui/src/engine/host.ts — startHost() spawns spec.command/spec.args with cwd=workspace, kill() ends stdin then child.kill() after 1500 ms; tui/src/app.tsx — '/exit' handler calls engine.shutdown() then exit().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a temp dir containing tui.mjs-like module and a sibling engine.cjs, isPackagedRun() returns true and resolveEngineSpawn('/ws') returns command === process.execPath, args deep-equal [<that dir>/engine.cjs, '--cwd', '/ws'] and env.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE === '1'.
2. Without a sibling engine.cjs, isPackagedRun() is false and resolveEngineSpawn falls back to command 'node' with args[0] === join(engineHome,'engine','host','dist','main.js') read from ~/.magentra-tui.json (point HOME/USERPROFILE at a temp dir and pre-write the config).
3. In dev mode with a config whose engineHome has no engine/host/dist/main.js, loadConfig() throws an Error whose message names both the missing main.js path and the config file path.
4. In dev mode with no config file at all, loadConfig() creates ~/.magentra-tui.json containing an engineHome key (best guess = repo root two levels above tui/src) instead of failing silently.
5. Spawn a fake engine script (a small node program that echoes a session_started frame and exits when stdin closes) through startHost(); calling kill() ends the child's stdin and the child process exits with exitCode !== null within 2 seconds, proving '/exit' tears the engine down and never leaves an orphan.
